name: alert, confirm and prompt dialogs
plain: Blocks the page with a modal alert, confirm or prompt box.
meaning: A site can interrupt the person with a message or a text box. Dialogs freeze the page script, are easy to abuse, and are blocked in cross-origin iframes and background tabs.

access.persistence: One-shot; Chrome adds Prevent this page from creating more dialogs after repeats
access.revocation: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)
access.iframe: Blocked in cross-origin iframes in Chrome 92 and later; sandboxed frames need allow-modals
steps: Browser shows modal dialog and blocks the page thread
Return value goes back to script

limits.headline: Can freeze the page with a pop up message box until you answer it
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page runs a script, or after an action like Delete.
can: Show an alert, a yes or no question or a box asking you to type text
Pause the page until you tap OK or Cancel
Ask Are you sure you want to leave? before you close the tab
cannot: Show the box on tabs you are not looking at in most browsers
Pause other tabs or other apps
Fill your screen with endless boxes; browsers let you block more from that page
See what you type into other sites
limits.reach_label: One page, one box at a time

story.what_it_is: A site can pop up a message box that freezes the page until you click.
story.for_you: You see a grey box that says something like 'Leave site?' or 'Are you sure?' and the page stops until you answer. Scam sites use fake versions to scare you.
story.for_makers: Makers use these for the simplest possible yes or no and for quick debugging. Browsers now limit them, so serious apps build their own dialogs instead.

use_cases.example: An online editor asks 'Discard unsaved changes?' when you try to close the tab.
A checkout page asks 'Are you sure you want to leave? Your cart will be lost.'
A fake 'Your computer is infected, call this number' alert loops on a scam site until you force quit.
A developer drops quick alert boxes into code to see a value while testing.
A simple browser game confirms 'Restart level?' before wiping your progress.
An old internal admin tool asks 'Delete 40 records?' with a plain browser confirm box.

technical_bounds: Cross-origin iframe dialogs are blocked in Chrome 92 (and Safari, Firefox have similar restrictions); same-origin iframes still allowed
Dialogs from background tabs are queued until the tab is foregrounded in Chrome
Chrome shows a Prevent this page from creating more dialogs checkbox on repeated dialogs
Dialog text is plain text, no HTML; Chrome shows the origin in the title
Modal blocks the whole event loop of the tab (and other same-process tabs may freeze)

abuse: Dialog loops that trap the tab

history.change: Cross-origin iframe alert, confirm, prompt blocked
Dialog from background tab queued; tab-modal dialogs introduced earlier
